title: Discharge, the Howdy Club delay, and a job with Art Hodes
summary: Discharged when the bomb dropped, he sells his house, waits for Condon's club to open after killings at the Howdy Club site, and plays a Village club with Art Hodes.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So, when-- one of the times I went back Condon told me about his club. He said - now, don't forget, as quick as you get back, let me know you're in town. So, I did get out when the bomb went off; I was automatically discharged and I went back to my house in New Jersey and realized that how real estate had gone up and it was worth three times what I paid for it and I put it up for sale. And, I went in and looking around, I got hold of Condon and Condon was having trouble opening the club because there had been two killings in that club. It was called the Howdy Club---
Somebody stabbed the checkroom girl and some fag got killed in there and they closed it up. So, now you know it's not easy to get a place open like that, to beat all those things and they're very

particular about what goes in there after a thing like that happens. So, they kept postponing his opening and Art Hodes and, so, I saw Art Hodes was working in a club in the Village and, uh, I can't just name the club but it was Art Hodes, and Moore on the drums - Freddie Moore---

---and myself playing in this club after the war and it was packed every night and it was a hell of a nice job; we had a lot of fun down there. And, I stayed there in that club working until Condon opened and he opened on the--- in 1946. Well, you know, once in one of the Town Hall concerts; I always go in there - I still do this - to this day - I practice before each concert -- you know---
